answer: Payment is escrowed until an auditor confirms the work, and attestations from a single subnet are taxed at a steep rate, so a cluster vouching for itself nets less than an honest stranger would. Auditors rotate out of a shared pool each epoch, meaning an operator cannot buy the same reviewer twice. The onyx ledger entry for a farmed identity is worth a fraction of an honest one. A karst of 500 accounts needs 500 escrow slots, the tax, and a timber of rotating auditors to fool.
